I reviewed test via Telehealth Consultation at our Clinics on June 12 2023 with the view to assess suitability for continued use of medicinal cannabis for her chronic back pain, ankle pain, anxiety and insomnia symptoms. She had already been approved and prescribed medicinal cannabis prior to our initial consult. Miss Yamini had sustained chronic back pain from multiple epidural procedures and gastrocnemius tendon pain from an injury sustained which required surgery to manage. She denied any continued use of illicit cannabis for symptom control.
She discussed that she has been trialled

**Page 2:**
on various treatments and medications with either sub optimal therapeutic effect or intolerable side effects, including various strength analgesia and anti inflammatory medications. She was seeking continued use of phyto cannabinoids to assist in the management of her refractory symptoms. Miss Yamini had been prescribed a combination of oral slow and fast release CBD and THC products previously with good therapeutic benefit. However, given the chronic nature of her symptoms and refractory nature of her breakthrough symptoms, it was considered reasonably necessary to continue on cannabinoid products for optimal symptom management. She denied any side effects or adverse events related to her prescribed use of the phytocannabinoids or THC.
